transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-12-05 15:00 UTC | Duration: 42m | Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Redwood SE), Maria Gomez (PulseSearch), Daniel Kim (PulseSearch), Ravi Narayanan (PulseSearch), Ellen Park (PulseSearch)

Summary (auto): Quick hosted API walkthrough showing embeddings generation, candidate retrieval and Redwood's rerank endpoint that applies cross-encoder scoring. Discussed latency tradeoffs, batch sizing, caching, and security controls. Agreed to POC scoping next week.

00:00 - Alex Chen: Alright folks, thanks for joining, um we really appreciate the time. I'm Alex, AE on the account, with Priya and Jordan from our SE team. Could we do quick intros from PulseSearch?
00:10 - Maria Gomez: Yep, I'm Maria, head of search, I own relevance. We have Daniel, Ravi and Ellen here too. We're trying to improve product search recall and reduce surfacing of wrong variants.
00:20 - Alex Chen: Great. Goal for today is a short demo of hosted embeddings + rerank, show typical end-to-end flow and call out latency/cost, then align on next steps. Sound ok?
00:28 - Maria Gomez: Yes that sounds good.
00:33 - Priya Patel: Cool, I'll share my screen and start with the embeddings endpoint. (screen shared) So Redwood hosted embeddings supports dense vectors from a few open models, we also surface verified performance per model in the console. We'll run a small snippet that generates 768-d vectors for product titles.
01:02 - Daniel Kim: Quick q, is the embedding returned normalized by default or do we need to normalise client-side?
01:08 - Priya Patel: Good question — we return raw floats; we recommend L2 normalize at query time for cosine similarity unless you use our vector store integrations where we normalize for you.
01:22 - Jordan Lee: (typing) I'm running the sample that we've linked in the deck, first up we call /v1/embeddings with model=redwood-embed-fast, here's the payload...
01:35 - Maria Gomez: Can you show latencies for that call?
01:40 - Jordan Lee: Sure — looks like 35 to 60ms per embed in our region for single-item calls. For bulk requests we can batch up to 64 items in a single request — throughput increases but per-item latency varies.
02:05 - Ravi Narayanan: Our SLA target for web results is under 120ms end-to-end, so how would reranking fit? If we do nearest-neighbor then rerank, that adds extra hops.
02:17 - Priya Patel: Totally. Typical pattern: do a fast ANN lookup (client or managed store) with embeddings to get candidates, then call Redwood's rerank endpoint which takes those candidates and the query and returns a scored list. We optimize the rerank model for short context and it returns in ~40-90ms depending on model size. Combined with cached embeddings and small candidate set you can often be <120ms.
02:45 - Daniel Kim: Is that 40-90ms from the hosted API for the cross-encoder style reranker?
02:50 - Priya Patel: Yes, for hosted dedicated small-medium models. For the 'redwood-rerank-small' we see ~45ms median in our US region. There is also a tiny variant optimized for <30ms with some quality tradeoffs.
03:05 - Maria Gomez: What's the cost delta between doing a cheap vector re-rank versus a more heavyweight cross-encoder?
03:12 - Alex Chen: Cost depends on tokens processed and model. We typically show per-call pricing for rerank endpoints; the cross-encoder will cost more per-request than a simple similarity score, but it gives better precision on tough queries. We'll include tiered pricing in the sheet.
03:30 - Ellen Park: Do you support re-ranking where we pass in metadata (e.g., price, availability) and have the reranker consider business rules?
03:38 - Priya Patel: Yes — our rerank endpoint accepts candidate metadata and we can condition the scoring prompt to include those attributes. You can also combine rule-based filters client-side before calling rerank to reduce token cost.
03:50 - Jordan Lee: I'm switching to the console to show per-route metrics. (screen) Here you can see token counts, latency per model, and a breakdown by route. You can also set a policy to fallback to a cheaper model if the high-quality model is unavailable.
04:20 - Maria Gomez: How do you handle model fallbacks in-hosted? We have peak traffic spikes.
04:26 - Jordan Lee: Smart routing — requests can be routed by cost/latency policy, and we support automatic fallback to model variants or regions. For spikes we recommend a burst policy and skyline autoscaling.
04:38 - Ravi Narayanan: Any caching options? We do a lot of repeated queries for popular SKUs.
04:42 - Priya Patel: Yes, Redwood supports prefix/KV caching for generation and caching embeddings at the client or managed caching layer; caching typically cuts downstream rerank calls for exact repeats. Also recommend warm-up for hot endpoints.
05:00 - Daniel Kim: If we store embeddings in our vector DB, do you have managed integrations?
05:05 - Jordan Lee: We have connectors for primary vector stores and recommend using an ANN service for fast nearest-neighbor; many customers use Pinecone, Milvus, or FAISS on their infra. Redwood also offers a managed store as an add-on.
05:20 - Maria Gomez: Security questions — can you confirm SOC2, SSO and encryption at rest? Also we need audit logs for queries tied to users.
05:30 - Priya Patel: Yes — we are SOC2 certified, support SAML/SSO and RBAC. Data at rest is encrypted with customer-managed KMS on Private deployments; for hosted we offer encryption and audit logs; we'll share the full security pack.
05:50 - Alex Chen: We'll attach the security PDF after the call. Priya can add the network diagram and data retention controls.
05:58 - Maria Gomez: Also do you retain query text? We need options for data retention and opt-out for logs.
06:04 - Priya Patel: Hosted can be configured with short retention windows; for strict regulatory needs we recommend Private deployment. We'll outline options in the docs.
06:15 - Daniel Kim: For the demo, can you show an end-to-end example: query -> embeddings -> candidates -> rerank -> final ordering?
06:22 - Jordan Lee: Yup, I'll run a small example against a toy product catalog. (runs) Ok, first we call embeddings for the query 'women's red rain jacket' and product titles to build vectors.
07:00 - 07:05 - (clip) Jordan Lee: Running ANN lookup returns 12 candidates — here's the top 5 by cosine.
07:10 - Priya Patel: Now we call Redwood rerank with those 12 candidates and the query, including metadata fields price and in_stock flag. Payload looks like client sends: {query, candidates: [{id, title, description, metadata}...]}
07:30 - Maria Gomez: Any sample rate limits or best practices for payload sizes?
07:35 - Priya Patel: Keep candidate sets small (10-50) to balance cost and accuracy. We have per-route rate limits; for POC we can raise quotas. If you need throughput we recommend batching and asynchronous pipelines.
07:55 - Jordan Lee: Rerank result returned — you can see it reorders items, pushes out-of-stock lower and elevates better matching product variants. Median rerank time here 52ms.
08:20 - Ravi Narayanan: That looks promising. How deterministic is rerank? Do we get consistent ordering across calls?
08:28 - Priya Patel: Rerank is deterministic for same payload/model version; if you use temperature or sampling it can vary. We recommend deterministic settings for ranking. Also pin model versions in rollout config to prevent sudden changes.
08:45 - Maria Gomez: What about A/B tests and rollouts? We want to test rerank changes on a subset of traffic.
08:50 - Jordan Lee: Console supports canary and A/B rollouts by route, you can set traffic splits and compare per-route metrics like CTR, latency and unit cost. We also offer quality regressions tied to prompt sets.
09:10 - Daniel Kim: For initial POC we want to run 10k queries and compare Redwood rerank vs our current heuristic. Can you do a batch eval?
09:18 - Priya Patel: Absolutely — we'll provide a small eval harness and a sample notebook. You can run locally or we can run a benchmark on a Redwood test project. We'll share the sample CSV and code.
09:35 - Maria Gomez: On pricing — we need to understand per-call cost for embedding + rerank and estimated monthly cost at 5M queries.
09:45 - Alex Chen: I'll calculate a couple scenarios and send a spreadsheet. We'll show hosted pricing for embeddings + rerank and include dedicated reserve options if you need predictable unit cost.
10:02 - Ellen Park: Any cold-starts or warm caches we should be aware of?
10:07 - Priya Patel: Cold-starts mainly happen on model variant spin-up; warm-up policies reduce that. For hosted we keep a pool warmed by default for higher tiers.
10:20 - Maria Gomez: Could you show how we would pass candidate metadata in the rerank request again?
10:25 - Jordan Lee: (shares snippet) Here: {query: "...", candidates: [{id:\"p1\", title:\"...\", metadata:{price:99.0, in_stock:true}}...], context_instructions: \"prefer in-stock, prefer 4+ star\"}. We also include a schema for metadata so the model knows attribute types.
10:55 - Daniel Kim: If we want to run rerank on a dedicated instance with our own private models, is that possible?
11:02 - Priya Patel: Yes — Dedicated or Private deployments let you pin models, use private model weights and integrate with your KMS. Private on-prem gives full data isolation. Hosted is easiest to start.
11:18 - Ravi Narayanan: What's the timeline if we want to go from POC to Dedicated?
11:22 - Alex Chen: Typically a few weeks to negotiate reserved capacity and a month to provision depending on region and capacity needs. We'll scope details after the POC.
11:35 - Maria Gomez: Any gotchas for multi-tenant data privacy if we use hosted?
11:40 - Priya Patel: Hosted isolates tenant data logically; we provide per-customer audit logs and access controls. For stricter isolation we recommend Dedicated or Private.
11:55 - Jordan Lee: I'm going to show the Optimize recommendations briefly — our tool suggests batching, quantization profiles for candidate models and caching rules that can reduce token costs by ~30% for typical search workloads.
12:20 - Maria Gomez: How do you measure quality regressions? We need alerts if rerank model drops relevance after a rollout.
12:26 - Priya Patel: We tie eval sets to alerting; the console will raise regression alerts when key metrics dip beyond thresholds and you can auto-rollback rollouts.
12:40 - Ellen Park: For the POC can you supply a small sample notebook that runs 10k queries and outputs an NDCG comparison?
12:50 - Jordan Lee: Yes — will attach the notebook and sample dataset.
13:05 - (longer demo silence as notebook runs)
18:10 - Jordan Lee: Results from small run: Redwood rerank improves NDCG by ~8-12% over baseline for product title queries in this sample. Caveat: model version and candidate quality matter.
18:35 - Daniel Kim: Nice. We should try with our actual catalog.
18:40 - Maria Gomez: Agreed. A couple of security follow-ups — need encryption in transit confirmation and role-based access control detail.
18:50 - Priya Patel: Encryption in transit is TLS 1.2+, and RBAC is configurable; we'll include the exact controls in the security pack.
19:05 - Ravi Narayanan: Do you have SSO examples for Okta? We use Okta and need SAML integration.
19:12 - Priya Patel: Okta SAML is supported; we have guides.
19:22 - Alex Chen: Quick recap — Action items: we'll send pricing and security docs, attach sample notebook and dataset, and schedule POC scoping next week. Any blockers on your side?
19:35 - Maria Gomez: No blockers. Daniel will own the POC and coordinate infra.
19:40 - Daniel Kim: Yep, I'll coordinate.
19:45 - Ellen Park: Can we get a written estimate for monthly cost for 5M queries?
19:50 - Alex Chen: Yes, I'll include scenario sheets.
19:55 - Jordan Lee: One more note — for heavy traffic we can recommend Dedicated with reserved capacity to lower per-call unit costs.
20:05 - Maria Gomez: Good to know.
20:10 - Alex Chen: Great, thanks everyone. We'll follow up with docs and schedule.

(End of transcript — transcription contains occasional mis-hears: 'KV cache' sometimes transcribed as 'KV cash', 'SOC2' transcribed as 'SOC two' in a few places, minor speaker swaps around interruptions.)
